text:
maya: Quick smoke run on the new int8 bring-up (heron-v2q) landed on dedicated — seeing intermittent structured-output parser failures in our tool-call suite. ~12/1000 invokes fail with 'missing required key: actions' even though the generation looks otherwise sane. Anyone seen boundary fragmentation with kvcache + int8? :eyes:

sam: Can you paste the raw response for one of the failures? That'll help narrow whether it's a generation truncation or a postprocess bug.

maya: Here's a sanitized raw example (copied from the capture):
```json
{
  "request_id": "r-9f3b",
  "meta": { "seed": 42, "model": "heron-v2q" },
  "result": [
    { "tool": "create_event", "params": { "title": "Sync" } }
  ]
}
```
Note: the expected contract is an object with top-level "actions" array. This payload looks like an accidental top-level array (and some other failures are truncated JSON where the closing field is stripped).

arjun: Hm. Two hypotheses: (1) streaming assembly / buffer boundary dropped a suffix when kvcache prefix was used, causing a partial payload, or (2) an int8 tokenizer/kernel edge case produced an unexpected token that our postproc mistakenly maps into a different structural shape. Is fp16 baseline hitting this?

maya: fp16 baseline is clean. Failures spike when batch_size >= 4 and when we enable prefix_kvcache. Also we're seeing higher rate when sequence length > 512.

tess: Try a quick isolation: disable kvcache for the canary and replay the same seeds, and also run the harness with a sentinel anchor that forces the model to emit an explicit terminator. Example canary command I ran for repros: 
```bash
./tools/canary-run --model heron-v2q --seed 42 --n 500 --batch 8 --capture raw --anchor "<END_OF_ACTIONS>"
```
And try bumping the client retry policy to linear-3 for now. If the failure rate drops to ~0 with kvcache disabled then that's a smoking gun.

infra-bot: canary-job 2026-03-03T15:12:45Z started: job_id cj-773, model=heron-v2q, nodes=2, batch=8. Logs will be at https://ci.internal/canary/cj-773 :construction_worker:

sam: I'll fork the harness and run two variants (kvcache on/off) against the same seed set. Also will capture raw token stream to check for truncated tail bytes. If we see consistent truncation points we'll correlate with kernel selection logs.

maya: thanks — doing a small staged rollout: disabling kvcache on the first canary wave and enabling the linear-3 retry_policy. I'll post results in this thread once the infra job finishes. If it's kvcache-induced, we should consider a short-term mitigation: automatic sentinel injection at append-time and a runtime check that rejects non-object top-level responses before postprocessing.

sam: good plan. If you want I can add a quick lint step in the postprocess that attempts a safe-wrap (objectify) then trigger a limited auto-retry to avoid downstream errors while we investigate.

maya: yes please. adding the lint+wrap as emergency patch. Will revert when root cause fixed. TY :)
